The sentence calls goal-lowering 'the corrective action' and says it does not close the gap.
findings.evidence: Deep 248 / source 1317-1324: 'One way to close this gap is to take corrective action, which, after time, improves actual performance. findings.fix: correct: Diagnosis: *Drifting Goals* — the gap was closed by lowering the goal rather than by corrective action that improves actual performance.

notes: All [V]-marked quotations match the converted source word for word except line 46 (clipped prompt, D009) and line 48 (bracketed substitutions, D010). Integration rows verified: Barbrook-Johnson seven methods, appropriateness triangle and Kim (2000) eight archetypes (bj deep 3, 7, 121, 285); four of SSDL's five archetypes appear by name in the Kim 2000 list and the fifth (limits to growth) as 'limits to success', so 'overlap heavily' holds; LFUO three foundational principles incl. Systems Thinking and Senge in Recommended Reading (lfuo deep 7, 13, 297); OB programmed/non-programmed, reflective/reactive, six barriers (ob deep 173-183); LS Agreement/Uncertainty Matrix (Stacey, Zimmerman) and Wicked Questions (ls deep 89, 107); Finance NPV and Economics utility for quantitative framing. Line 12's 'systems-thinking dimension that the prior corpus largely lacked' is an ungraded corpus-history remark. Worked example line 167 says 'three loops' but the third item is a stock, not a loop (internal, not a source claim). Applied extensions left ungraded: 'Adding a time delay?' at line 123 is not among the source's intervention moves (loops and links only), and the structural vs event cost comparison at line 125 is a generalisation of shifting-the-burden.
